title: Answers That Never End Explained Simply | PUC Maths Class 11
description:
When is a bicycle tyre valve exactly at half height? At 30 degrees on the way up, at 150 degrees on the way down, then again after every full turn, forever. One equation, endless answers. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 3, Trigonometric Functions) we learn to write every one of those answers in a single line. Note: trigonometric equations are not in the current rationalised NCERT text, but they are asked in JEE Main and JEE Advanced.

You will watch the solutions of sin x = 1/2 appear as dots on a live graph and count up turn after turn, then raise the line y = k and see the count drop to one per turn and then to zero. We build the general solution x = nπ + (-1)^n α step by step from the unit circle, meet the rules for cos x = cos α, tan x = tan α, sin x = 0 and cos x = 0, and compare principal and general solutions side by side. A pause-and-think question, a worked example (sin x = -√3/2), the exam trap with cos x = 1/2, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and JEE students.

In this video:
0:00 The valve at half height, again and again
0:32 What is a trigonometric equation?
0:55 Live: count the solutions on the graph
1:13 Raise the line: two, one, then zero per turn
1:31 Building the general solution of sin x = sin α
2:14 cos, tan and the zero cases
2:42 Principal vs general solutions
3:21 Worked example: sin x = -√3/2
4:00 Exam trap: cos x = 1/2
4:22 Where it is asked
4:31 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:03 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode (Ep 37): Need for Complex Numbers. x squared plus 1 equals 0, and no number on the number line works.
